name: Pollack
summary: German four-player partnership trick-taking game similar to Tresette where teams score for cards in tricks and hand combinations.
rules_text: Played with 32 cards, rank 10>9>A>K>Q>J>8>7. Use two partnerships of two opposite each other. Deal 8 cards each in 3-3-2. No trumps; must follow suit. Ace=3 points, K Q J 10 9 =1 each, 8 7=0. Last trick =3 points. Total card points divided by 3 ignoring fractions gives 11 points per deal. Before first trick forehand may announce, thereafter a team may announce only after winning a trick. Announcements: three Tens/Nines/Aces =3, four of same =4, Ten+Nine+Ace same suit (Pollack)=3. First team to 21 points wins a partie, but must announce upon reaching it on lead or after winning a trick; if they forget opponent can claim first. Play six parties. If both exceed 21 same deal, higher score wins, tie broken by last trick.
rating_reason: Team trick-taking with bonuses, point scoring
